about: About these leads

Leaflegal sends family law enquiries from people in England and Wales who want to pay a solicitor to help with a separation, divorce, money or children matter. Each enquiry goes to one firm only. It is never sent to several firms at once and it is never resold after delivery.

People usually contact a family solicitor at one of the hardest points in their life. A relationship has ended, a former partner has made a proposal about money, a court form has arrived or arrangements for the children have broken down. They want to understand where they stand and they often want to speak to someone the same day.

Since legal aid was withdrawn for most private family matters, the great majority of these clients pay privately. Every Leaflegal family enquiry has confirmed that the person is looking for paid help rather than legal aid or free advice, so your first call starts from that shared understanding.

Our campaigns run on social media, search and helpful content aimed at people going through a separation. Each person answers a short set of questions about the kind of help they need, whether anything has started at court, how urgent it is and where they are. When the enquiry fits the matter types and areas you have chosen, we check it and send it to you straight away.

about.h3: Why exclusive matters in family work

about: Family clients are choosing someone to guide them through something personal and painful. If they are called by four firms within an hour, the experience can feel overwhelming, and the firm that wins is often simply the one that called first. Sending each enquiry to one firm gives you room to have a proper, unhurried conversation and to show the client why they should trust you.

Leaflegal is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. We do not comment on a client's options or tell them what to expect from a settlement or a court. We introduce them to one regulated firm, and the advice comes from you.
Who enquires

Family enquiries cover a wide range of work. You choose which matter types you want, so a practice built around complex financial remedy work does not have to take simple uncontested divorces unless it wants them.

list: Divorce and dissolution of a civil partnership
Cohabitation disputes, including property disputes between unmarried couples

about.h3: Where they are in the process

about: Some people enquire before they have told their partner they want to separate. Others have already started an online divorce and now need help with the finances. Some have received a court application or a letter from the other side's solicitor and need someone quickly. Each lead says whether proceedings have started and whether there is a hearing date, so you can tell the difference before you call.

Since no fault divorce came in, more people start the divorce themselves and come to a solicitor for the finances or the children. Many of the enquiries you receive will therefore be about money or arrangements for children, alongside straightforward divorce work.

about.h3: What clients want from the first call

about: Most family clients want three things early on. They want to feel listened to, they want a clear explanation of what usually happens next, and they want to know what it might cost. People are often frightened about fees running out of control, so a fixed fee first meeting or a clear estimate for the first stage helps them say yes.

Clients also differ in how much they already know. Some have read widely and arrive with specific questions about pensions or the family home. Others know very little and need the basics explained gently. The description in the client's own words usually gives a good sense of which kind of conversation to expect.

Not every enquiry is a crisis. Couples planning a wedding or civil partnership enquire about prenuptial agreements, and separated couples who get on well ask about separation agreements or consent orders. These clients are usually calmer and often want a fixed price for a defined piece of work.
Lead details

Every family lead is the full record of what the client told us, in the order they told us. We keep the questions short because the subject is sensitive, but each lead gives your team enough to make a well prepared first call.

list: The client's name, a verified UK mobile number and a verified email address
Whether the matter is about divorce, finances, children or something else
How urgent it is and any hearing date they know about
Confirmation that they want paid help, not legal aid
A short description in the client's own words
The best time to call, which matters when someone may not be able to talk freely at home
The source, a timestamp and the consent record

about.h3: A note on the best time to call

about: In family matters, the time and way you contact someone can matter more than usual. A client may still live with their partner or may not want to be overheard. Each lead includes the best time to call, and it is worth respecting that closely. If a client does not pick up, a short, discreet message usually works better than a detailed voicemail.

Every client confirms they want paid help with a family matter in England and Wales, and their mobile number and email address are checked. Enquiries that fall outside our scope or your criteria are filtered out and the person is pointed somewhere more suitable, so they never reach you.

Each client ticks one box to confirm they understand our terms, our privacy policy and that Leaflegal is an introduction service, and a separate box to agree to one firm contacting them by phone, email or text. We record the wording and the time and send it with the lead. Leads arrive as soon as they are checked, by email, to a shared inbox or into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook.
Working the lead
Family enquiries reward firms that respond quickly and with warmth. People contact a solicitor at a moment of crisis, and the first voice they hear often shapes who they instruct.

Aim to call soon after a lead arrives, at the time the client asked for. A same day call shows that you take their situation seriously. Where a lead mentions a hearing date or a court application, route it to a fee earner who can deal with urgent work.

Use what the client has already told us. Opening with a reference to their situation, such as a recent separation and a question about the house, shows you have read their enquiry and lets them talk. Many family clients need to tell their story before they can take in information about process or cost.

A fixed fee first meeting, or a clear estimate for the first stage of the work, makes it easier for anxious clients to commit. Explain what they will get from that meeting and what they might bring, in general terms. Be honest that later costs depend on how the matter unfolds.

The client agreed to be contacted after making an enquiry through Leaflegal. Mention that early in the call, and cover any referral arrangement in your client care letter as the SRA Code of Conduct requires.

Some clients are not ready to instruct straight away. They may be waiting to see how a conversation with their partner goes, or saving for fees. A kind follow up email and a second call a few days later is often welcome. Keep the tone supportive rather than sales led.

Let us know which leads instruct and which do not. If contested finances convert well for you but simple divorce enquiries do not, we can change your matching so you receive more of the work you want.

Firms that look at their results every month or so, and share what they see with us, usually find it easier to shape the mix of family work they receive. Small changes, such as adjusting areas or switching off one matter type, can make a real difference to how well the leads fit your team.
Compliance
Family work raises particular compliance points because clients are often vulnerable and the information they share is sensitive. Leaflegal is set up to support your professional duties.

Leaflegal is an introducer. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement you have with an introducer, and that the arrangement does not affect your independence or your advice. Our consent wording tells every client we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with each lead so your client care letter can match it.

Family enquiries go to SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work. You remain responsible for your own conflict checks, which matter a great deal in family law because you cannot act for both sides. If you find you already act for the other party, do not take the matter on and let us know.

Family enquiries can include information about health, children and sometimes allegations of abuse. We keep our questions to the minimum needed for first contact and never pass matter details to advertising platforms. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms. Once a lead is delivered, you are controller of your copy and handle it under your own privacy notice.

Some clients will be in distress or in difficult situations at home. Your own policies on vulnerable clients and safeguarding apply in the usual way. The best time to call field is there partly so you can contact people safely.
Read more about referral rules and introducers.
Pricing

You pay for each family lead we deliver, at a price agreed with you before you start. There is no retainer for advertising and no shared or recycled data, so you can measure every lead against the instructions it produces.

Price depends on the matter types and locations you choose. A contested financial matter is usually worth more to a firm than a simple uncontested divorce, and a narrow area around one office produces fewer matches than wider coverage. We talk this through on a call and put a proposal together for your firm.

The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you tell us how many your team can handle and we match to that number. You can set a monthly cap, change it and pause at any time, for example during a busy trial period or when a fee earner is on leave.

Before your first lead, we agree a written partner agreement covering pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads. If a lead has wrong contact details or falls outside your agreed criteria, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says.

Onboarding starts with a 30 minute call with our team. We talk about the family work you handle, the areas you cover and how many leads you can take, and we show you a sample lead before you commit. You can apply to become a partner firm to book the call.
faqs: The leads
What is a family law lead from Leaflegal?

It is an enquiry from a person in England and Wales who wants to pay a solicitor to help with a family matter, such as a divorce, finances on separation or arrangements for children. They have told us the type of matter, whether proceedings have started, how urgent it is and where they are, confirmed their contact details and agreed to be contacted by one firm.
Are family leads exclusive?

Yes. Each enquiry goes to one firm only and is never resold. We do not send the same person to several firms at once, which matters in family work because people at a difficult time can find several calls from competing firms overwhelming. You are the only firm that receives the client's details from us, so you have space for a proper first conversation.
Do family clients pay privately?

Yes. Every client confirms they want paid help rather than legal aid or free advice. Legal aid for most private family matters was withdrawn some years ago, so most people now pay privately. If someone tells us they only want legal aid, they are pointed elsewhere and do not become a lead. Your first call can therefore start from that shared understanding.
Which family matters can I receive?

You can choose from divorce and dissolution, financial settlements and consent orders, child arrangements, cohabitation disputes, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements and separation agreements. You can take all of them or only the work your team wants. Many firms focus on financial and children work and leave simpler matters out, while others welcome fixed fee divorce work.
Will I know if court proceedings have started?

Yes. Each lead says whether proceedings have started and whether there is a hearing date the client knows about. That helps you tell the difference between someone planning ahead and someone who has just received a court application, so you can route the urgent ones to a fee earner who can act quickly and plan the rest around your diary.
What does the best time to call mean for family leads?

Each client tells us when it is best to call. In family matters this can be important, because a client may still live with their partner or may not want to be overheard. Respecting that time, and leaving a short and discreet message if they do not answer, helps the client feel safe and makes it more likely they will speak openly.
Do you send enquiries from both parties to the same firm?

We match each enquiry on its own, and we cannot always know whether two enquiries relate to the same relationship. That is why your own conflict checks remain essential. If you find that you already act for the other party, do not take the matter on and let us know. We will treat the lead as your partner agreement sets out.
Do you send enquiries about domestic abuse or emergency protection?

Our family enquiries focus on privately funded separation, money and children matters. Some clients will mention difficult circumstances in their own words, and you should handle those leads with your usual care. Legal aid can be available for some people affected by domestic abuse, so if a client turns out to qualify and prefers that route, your normal approach to signposting applies.
Volume and areas
How many family leads will I receive?

That depends on the matter types and locations you choose and the enquiries our campaigns are generating at the time. The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you set the number your team can handle and we match to it. We will give you an honest view on your call of what is realistic, but we cannot promise a fixed number.
Can I choose the areas I cover?

Yes. You can choose towns, counties or regions, a radius around your offices, or the whole of England and Wales if you work remotely. Many family clients like to meet their solicitor in person at least once, so some firms prefer local clients. Others work by video across the country. Wider coverage usually means more matches.
Can I choose only financial or children work?

Yes. Each family matter type can be switched on or off. If your firm focuses on financial remedy work and complex children cases, you can leave out simple divorces and prenuptial agreements. If you run a fixed fee divorce service, you can ask for more of that work. You can change the mix whenever you like.
Can I set a monthly cap?

Yes. You set the number of leads you want each month, as long as it is at least the minimum of 10. When you reach your cap, we stop matching enquiries to you until the next month. You can change your cap whenever your capacity changes, so your team is never sent more enquiries than it can call back promptly.
Can I pause my leads?

Yes. If your team is at capacity, a key fee earner is away or you are preparing for a long hearing, tell us and we will pause matching until you are ready. Pausing does not end your partner agreement. When you want to restart, let us know and matching begins again as new enquiries come in.
Can leads go to different fee earners?

Yes. We can route leads by matter type or location, so financial enquiries go to one team and children matters to another. We can also send everything to a shared intake inbox or your CRM, where you assign each lead to the right person. We set up whatever suits the way your family team works.
Do you send enquiries from outside England and Wales?

No. Family law enquiries come from people with a matter in England and Wales. Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own family law systems, so we do not send those enquiries. Within England and Wales, the number of leads you receive depends on the areas you choose, the matter types you switch on and the volume of enquiries at the time.
Compliance
Do I need to disclose the referral fee to clients?

Yes. The SRA Code of Conduct requires you to make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement you have with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence. Our consent wording tells every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with every lead so your client care letter can match it.
Does Leaflegal give family law advice?

No. Leaflegal is an introduction service, not a law firm. We do not comment on a client's options, what a settlement might look like or what a court might decide. We tell every client this before they submit their enquiry. All advice comes from your firm once you are in contact with the client.
How is sensitive information handled?

Family enquiries can touch on health, children and sometimes abuse. We keep our questions to the minimum needed for first contact and never pass matter details to advertising platforms. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms, and once a lead is delivered you become controller of your copy under your own privacy notice.
How is client consent recorded?

Each client ticks one box confirming they have read our terms and privacy policy and understand that Leaflegal is an introduction service, and a second box agreeing to their details being shared with one firm that may contact them by phone, email or text. We record the exact wording and the time, and that record arrives with the lead.
What about vulnerable clients?

Some family clients will be distressed or in a difficult situation at home. Your own policies on vulnerable clients and safeguarding apply as they would to any new client. The best time to call field helps you contact people safely, and a short, discreet first message is often the most considerate approach when a call goes unanswered.
Can I add family clients to a mailing list?

Only with their separate consent. The consent given through Leaflegal covers contact about the client's enquiry. If you would like to send newsletters or other marketing, you need to ask for that permission yourself and follow your privacy notice and UK data protection law. Many family clients prefer not to receive marketing, so asking clearly matters.
Pricing and terms
How much does a family law lead cost?

There is no published price list. You pay per lead at a price agreed with you before you start, based on the matter types and locations you choose and the volume you want. We put a proposal together after your onboarding call, so you know the cost of every lead before the first one is delivered.
Is there a written agreement?

Yes. Your partner agreement covers pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads, and it is in place before your first lead. Both sides know from the start what is charged, how leads are counted and how any problem with a lead is handled. We go through it with you and answer any questions before you sign.
What counts as an invalid lead?

Your partner agreement sets this out. It usually covers things like wrong contact details or an enquiry outside your agreed criteria. If you think a lead is invalid, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says. A client deciding not to instruct does not by itself make a lead invalid.
What if the client is not ready to instruct?

Many family clients need time. They may be waiting for a conversation with their partner, gathering information or saving for fees. A lead is an introduction rather than a guaranteed instruction. A warm follow up email and a second call a few days later often help, and sharing your results with us helps us shape the leads you receive.
Getting started
How do I become a partner firm?

Apply to become a partner firm and book a 30 minute call with our team. We go through the family work you handle, your locations, your regulation and the volume you can take. Then we agree your criteria and price, show you a sample lead and put your partner agreement in place before any leads are sent.
Can I see a sample family lead?

Yes. On your call we show you a sample family lead with every field, the format it arrives in and the consent record. You can see exactly what your team would receive, including the best time to call and whether proceedings have started, before you decide whether to go ahead.
Is there a portal to log into?

No. There is no platform and no login. Leads arrive by email, to a shared intake inbox or straight into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook. Your team works them in the systems they already use, so nothing is missed in a separate tool.
What should we set up before our first lead?

Decide who will call new family leads and how quickly, and who covers lunchtimes and late afternoons. Send leads to a shared inbox or CRM rather than one person. Prepare a short explanation of your first meeting and its cost, and check that your client care letter covers the referral arrangement as the SRA Code requires.
Can we change our matching after we start?

Yes. Your criteria are not fixed. If you take on a new family fee earner, open another office or decide you want more financial remedy work and fewer simple divorces, tell us and we update your matching. Sharing which leads instruct, and why others do not, helps us send you more of the work that suits your team.
